teaser.text: KKR is a financial company that earns money by managing other people’s investments, selling insurance promises and owning selected businesses. To understand how a dollar comes in and goes out, follow three connected businesses: Asset Management, Global Atlantic insurance and Strategic Holdings.

blocks.heading: Where could KKR’s shares go in each scenario?

paragraphs.text: KKR’s weighted path reaches $110.43 in October 2029, or +31% including dividends, if fee growth, successful realizations and replacement USI earnings arrive. Management guides to Insurance Operating Earnings of $250 million per quarter in the second half of 2026 and Strategic Holdings Operating Earnings of at least $350 million for 2026. The regular annualized common dividend is guided at $0.78 per share. KKR expects $3,300 million of after-tax proceeds and $2,000 million of Adjusted Net Income from the USI sale in 2026.

The weighted forecast is $86.59 in October 2027, or +1%. Probabilities are 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull. At October 2029, outcomes range from $41.45 in the bear case (-50%) to $217.44 in the bull case (+155%); the base case is $109.01 (+29%).

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for KKR?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the main earnings bridge. The base case uses $5,500 million at the first date and $6,100 million at the middle date. It reaches $6,700 million at the final date. The bear path starts at $4,700 million and ends at $5,400 million; the bull path starts at $6,200 million and ends at $8,200 million. The base begins above 2025 Adjusted Operating Income because FPAUM grew to $604,144 million and insurance operating earnings reached $1,109.395 million by 2025. Fundraising and deployment support the bull case, while the USI sale and difficult exits support the bear case.

The USI closing expected in 2027 is the central hinge: proceeds support the base balance sheet, but failure to replace its future earnings would push the forecast toward bear. Conversely, strong exits, durable fundraising, rising insurance earnings and efficient Gen II expansion would move the assumptions toward bull.

blocks.heading: How much cash does KKR really make?

paragraphs.text: The apparent calculation is simple: cash from operations less capital spending produces free cash flow, and subtracting stock compensation produces a still lower figure. But KKR consolidates investment funds whose purchases and sales enter operating cash flow. That money may belong economically to fund investors, not to KKR’s shareholders.

blocks.heading: How much does KKR pay shareholders?

paragraphs.text: KKR’s weighted path reaches $110.43 in October 2029, or +31% including dividends, if fee growth, successful realizations and replacement USI earnings arrive. Management guides to Insurance Operating Earnings of $250 million per quarter in the second half of 2026 and Strategic Holdings Operating Earnings of at least $350 million for 2026. The regular annualized common dividend is guided at $0.78 per share. KKR expects $3,300 million of after-tax proceeds and $2,000 million of Adjusted Net Income from the USI sale in 2026.

Dividends rise from $0.82 to $0.90 in the base case. The bear case holds the current $0.78 guidance initially before cutting to $0.70, while the bull case reaches $1.04. The base increase is below the recent dividend-growth record because carry is uneven and USI’s future earnings must be replaced.

blocks.heading: Is KKR’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The apparent calculation is simple: cash from operations less capital spending produces free cash flow, and subtracting stock compensation produces a still lower figure. But KKR consolidates investment funds whose purchases and sales enter operating cash flow. That money may belong economically to fund investors, not to KKR’s shareholders.
A better cash test follows fees collected, realized carry after employee participation, dividends, permitted insurer distributions, corporate interest and cash taxes.

earnings.title: KKR earnings date and guidance
earnings.meta_description: KKR reports next on November 9, 2026; guidance covers insurance, Strategic Holdings, the dividend and USI proceeds.
earnings.opening: KKR’s next results are expected on November 9, 2026. Watch whether KKR can turn investment activity into dependable earnings and usable liquidity.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains KKR’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: The remaining guidance is narrower. Insurance Operating Earnings are guided at $250 million per quarter in the second half of 2026. Strategic Holdings Operating Earnings are guided at a minimum of $350 million for the year. The regular annualized common dividend is $0.78 a share. These are different scorecards, not figures to add together.

USI, an insurance brokerage, makes the distinction sharper. KKR expects $3.3 billion of after-tax proceeds from its sale. It expects $2 billion of Adjusted Net Income from the transaction, including at least $2 per share. USI supplies 40.0% of expected 2026 Strategic Holdings Operating Earnings, so its sale also removes an established contributor. The remaining 18 companies must help replace it before the segment can reach management’s longer-term target of more than $1.1 billion in 2030.

blocks.heading: Has KKR kept its fundraising promise?

paragraphs.text: KKR also targeted more than US$300 billion of fundraising over 2024–2026 and had raised US$305 billion by June 2026. That delivery matters, but the final test is value created for each share after paying the people who created it.

blocks.heading: What do KKR’s last eight quarters show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue and net income rose while operating income fell. That divergence shows why the bottom line cannot stand in for operating progress. A securities impairment before sale reduced operating income; removing it changes the quarter from an operating decline to growth. Corporate costs provide another alternative view, but their narrower components are already included in the subtotal.

blocks.heading: What should KKR watch on November 9, 2026?

paragraphs.text: The scheduled third-quarter results call is November 9, 2026, at 10 a.m. Eastern. Investors should compare actual realizations with July’s visibility, then examine fundraising, deployment and the remaining operating guidance. A sale delayed into the fourth quarter is different from a cancelled transaction or a lower sale price.
